               <ns0:p n="23">23 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 5.25.</ns0:note> I beheld <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Either I <ns0:hi>Ieremiah</ns0:hi> saw all this in a vision, or I fancied and framed such an <ns0:hi>Idea</ns0:hi> of it in my mind, it seems to be impres<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sed upon my thoughts <ns0:hi>Graphically,</ns0:hi> as in a Map, in such a rue<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful manner; for in this, and the three following verses, he doth as one transported with sorrow, elegantly, and <ns0:hi>hyperbolically</ns0:hi> de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />scribe the <ns0:hi>Phaenomenon,</ns0:hi> face or appearance of it.</ns0:note> the earth, and Io, <ns0:hi>it was</ns0:hi> without form and void <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">The Land was so squallid, and so ruined, that he fancieth it to be like the first Chaos, for which reason possibly he calls <ns0:hi>Iudea</ns0:hi> the earth, in allusion to <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 1.2. and herein implying that <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi>'s sins were such, that they had even overturned the course of nature, being laid waste and desolate, not of inhabitants only, but of all things that might tend either to ornament or use, without men, without houses, without fruits, without beasts or birds for food or service, <ns0:hi>verse</ns0:hi> 25.26.</ns0:note>: and the heavens, and they <ns0:hi>had</ns0:hi> no light <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Some say being obnubila<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ted, and darkened by the abundance of smoke that would as<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cend from the desolating fires of Towns and Cities, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 9.18, 19. of which you may read in the History of this break<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing in of the <ns0:hi>Chaldees,</ns0:hi> but he seems to proceed rather in his <ns0:hi>Metaphor</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Chaos,</ns0:hi> and it being an expression, whereby the Scripture doth set forth the saddest desolations, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 13.9. <ns0:hi>&c.                <ns0:p n="24">24 I beheld the mountains, and lo, they trem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bled <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">He proceeds in his figurative elegancies, <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> behold how the Mountains of <ns0:hi>Iudea</ns0:hi> tremble!                   </ns0:note>, and all the birds of the heavens were fled <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Such birds as are used to inhabit places, that live, feed and build among men, others indeed, both birds and beasts would continue, which implies but the greater desola<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion, and wast of the Land, as is threatned against <ns0:hi>Babylon; Isa.</ns0:hi> 13.19, 20, 21, 22. either to seek provisions, here being no food left for them, or frighted with the hideous noises and clatterings that do attend Armies; as we have read, that such hath been the concussion of the Air by the loud clamours and noises of Armies, that birds have fallen down to the earth, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 9.10. <ns0:hi>Zeph.</ns0:hi> 1.2, 3.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 I beheld, and lo, the fruitful place <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>Carmel,</ns0:hi> either <ns0:hi>properly</ns0:hi> for that part of the Land so called for its fruitfulness, or rather <ns0:hi>Appellatively</ns0:hi> for, not only their most pleasant, but most fruitful Lands, that were kept dressed and occupied for food, both for necessity and delight, <ns0:hi>verse</ns0:hi> 27. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 29.17. and 33.9.</ns0:note>

               <ns0:p n="27">27 For thus hath the LORD said, the whole land shall be desolate; <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 5.10, 18. & 46.28.</ns0:note> yet will I not make a full end <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Some expound it, neither shall this punishment suffice, nor my fury stop here, I will not thus have done with them, and look to what they were further to endure in their long cap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tivity; see <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 26.36, 39. but it seems rather to be a word of comfort, that they shall not be utterly extinct, he will preserve a remnant, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 5.10. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 1.9. and 24.13. <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> Though I am greatly moved with anger, yet I will not be inexorable, I will remember my Covenant, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 30.11. in the midst of judgment he will remember mercy, after 70 years Captivity he brought them back again.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

               <ns0:p n="29">29 The whole city shall flee, for the noise <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Either upon the report of their coming, hereby as it were deriding their confidence, or rather at the approach of their vast Ar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mies, for they were close besieged before they fled, as appears 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 25.4.</ns0:note> of the horsemen and bowmen, they shall go in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to thickets <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Such a consternation there shall be upon them, that they shall run into every hole to hide themselves; thus <ns0:hi>Manasseh</ns0:hi> was taken among the thorns, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 33.11. the <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> is <ns0:hi>abim</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>clouds,</ns0:hi> possibly alluding to dark places on the tops of hills, reaching as it were to the clouds, or among the cloudy shades of Trees and Groves that usually grew there, the LXX render it <ns0:hi>Caves,</ns0:hi> and so the Rocks for shelter, or the clefts, Caves and hiding places in the Rocks, see <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 2.21.</ns0:note>, and climb up upon the rocks: e<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />very city <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">The inhabitants of all ranks and qualities shall seek to es<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cape the fury of this <ns0:hi>Chaldean</ns0:hi> Army, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 39.4.</ns0:note>
